paras: In addition, the Government's position assumes that there was a lawful and binding

after Epstein accepted the immunity offer. But the Government could not lawfully extend a valid offer until it had conferred with Epstein's victims. Accordingly, the Government attorneys were simply not authorized to propose immunity to Epstein when they did - and any alleged
agreement was invalid at its inception.
The Eleventh Circuit has made clear that "to enforce a promise made during plea negotiations, there must have been a valid, binding agreement in the first
. . . . For an agreement to be valid and binding, the agent must possess actual authority to make the promise . . . .
Estoppel and apparent authority normally will not substitute for
authority to bind the United States Government."
